content_units: Best-Fit Comedy Specials for Clever, Kind, Under-75 Viewing
Given your priorities, the strongest matches are the specials with sharp written structure, low reliance on crowd work, and a tone that stays more thoughtful or playful than mean.
Rank   Special   Runtime   Why it fits

1     John Mulaney: Kid Gorgeous     65m   Probably the cleanest match: highly crafted writing, strong storytelling rhythm, and a polished, joke-dense set without leaning on crowd interaction or cruelty.
2     Nate Bargatze: The Tennessee Kid     61m   Very strong if you want relaxed, tightly written material with an easygoing tone. It is especially good for avoiding mean-spirited humor.

3     Bo Burnham: Make Happy     60m   Extremely clever and formally inventive, with sharp writing and strong thematic construction. Ranked slightly lower only because its edge and self-aware intensity may be less cozy than the top two.
Option 1:   John Mulaney: Kid Gorgeous     Elegant joke writing and memorable storytelling with broad appeal   Best overall fit
Option 2:   Nate Bargatze: The Tennessee Kid     Gentle, smart, low-meanness comedy with efficient writing   Safest tonal pick
Option 3:   Bo Burnham: Make Happy     Smartest structural experimentation of the group, still under an hour   Best if you want inventive form
Option 4:   Hannah Gadsby: Douglas     Very smart and deliberate, with strong thematic callbacks and conceptual writing   Best backup if you want something more essay-like
- More cerebral and lecture-like in places, so it may be less immediately “comedy-special breezy” than Mulaney or Bargatze
Fit Notes on the Remaining Option

Ali Wong: Baby Cobra   is very funny and well-written, but for your stated preferences it lands slightly lower because its tone can feel more biting and aggressive than the others, even though it is not crowd-work heavy.
